τὰς διὰ τῶν ἁγίων θεοσημίας, ὁ αὐτὸς ἡμῖν ἀποπεραίνει Θεός· πάντα γὰρ, ὡς ἔφην, παρὰ
Πατρὸς δι' Υἱοῦ ἐν Πνεύματι, καὶ ἐφ' ἅπασι τοῖς κατορθουμένοις ἡ ἁγία καὶ ὁμοούσιος
Τριὰς δοξάζεται. ἄθρει γὰρ 288 ὅπως ἄρχεται μὲν ἀπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος ὡς ὄντος ἐν ἡμῖν
καὶ τὴν τῶν θείων χαρισμάτων ἐνεργοῦντος διανομήν· ἀναβιβάσας δὲ τὸν λόγον ἐπὶ
τὸν Υἱὸν, ὅς ἐστιν Υἱὸς κατὰ φύσιν, ἄνεισιν οὕτω λοιπὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πατέρα, τὴν διὰ τοῦ
Πνεύματος ἐνέργειαν διὰ μέσου τοῦ Υἱοῦ προσνέμων αὐτῷ.
Ἑτέρῳ δὲ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ Πνεύματι. Πίστις ἐν τούτοις εἴη ἂν, καθάπερ ἐγῷμαι,
ἡ πρὸς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἑδραιότης καὶ ὧν ἂν βούλοιτο Θεός· φαμὲν γὰρ οὕτω
γενέσθαι πιστὸν "ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ" τὸν ἱεροφάντην Μωσέα· οὐ γὰρ τὸ χρῆναι
πιστεῦσαι μόνον ὅτι φύσει καὶ ἀληθῶς εἷς ἐστι τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς, πίστις ἂν νοοῖτο καὶ
λέγοιτο, ἀλλὰ τὸ εὖ βεβηκέναι κατὰ ψυχὴν, "καὶ "ἕτοιμον εἶναι τοῦ πορεύεσθαι μετὰ
Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ" κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου φωνήν· καὶ γοῦν οἱ θεσπέσιοι μαθηταὶ
προσῄεσάν ποτε τῷ Χριστῷ λέγοντες ἐναργῶς "Πρόσθες "ἡμῖν πίστιν." δίδοται δὲ πρὸς
τούτῳ καὶ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ Πνεύματι. καί μοι πάλιν ἐπιτήρει λεπτῶς· τοῦ
γὰρ Πνεύματος διανέμειν λεγομένου τὰ τῶν ἰαμάτων χαρίσματα, Χριστός ἐστιν ὁ
διδούς· δέδωκε γὰρ τοῖς ἁγίοις ἀποστόλοις "ἐξουσίαν κατὰ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε
"ἐκβάλλειν αὐτά·" καὶ δὴ καὶ ἔφασκεν "Ἀσθενοῦντας θερα"πεύετε, καὶ νεκροὺς
ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, καὶ δαι"μόνια ἐκβάλλετε, δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε."
αὐτοῦ δὲ δὴ πάντως καὶ τὰ τῶν δυνάμεων ἐνεργήματα, πλὴν ἐν Πνεύματι τῷ ἑνί· οἷον
ἔῤῥιψεν ὁ Μωσῆς τὴν ῥάβδον εἰς γῆν καὶ γέγονεν ὄφις, μετεσκεύασεν εἰς αἷμα τοὺς
ποταμοὺς, ἐξήγαγεν ὕδωρ ἐκ πέτρας· τετελέκασι δὲ πλεῖστα ὅσα καὶ πέρα 289 λόγου καὶ
θαύματος οἱ μακάριοι προφῆται· ταῦτα δὲ εἶναί φαμεν τὰ τῶν δυνάμεων ἐνεργήματα δι'
ἑνὸς τοῦ Πνεύματος· ἀλλὰ καὶ προφητεύει τις ἕτερος, πλὴν οὐ δίχα τοῦ Πνεύματος· ἔχει
δέ τις καὶ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων, πλὴν ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ Πνεύματι· ποίων δὲ πνευμάτων,
εἴρηται πρότερον· διδόναι γεμὴν καὶ ἑτέροις ἰσχυρίζεται τὸ εἰδέναι γένη γλωσσῶν, καὶ
μέντοι καὶ ἑρμηνείας· χάρισμα δὲ τοῦτό φαμεν ἴδιον καὶ ἐν καιρῷ καὶ χρείᾳ τισὶν
οἰκονομικῶς κεχορηγημένον. Ἀλλ' οἱ μὲν ταῖς γλώσσαις ἐλάλουν, καίτοι πρὶν οὐκ
εἰδότες αὐτὰς, οἱ δὲ συνῆσαν διερμηνεύοντες καίτοι πάλαι τὸ οὖς οὐκ ἐντριβῆ τε καὶ ἐν
ἔθει τῶν τοιούτων ἐχόντων τινῶν· δεδόσθαι γεμὴν ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος τοῖς τὸ
τηνικάδε διισχυρίζεται τὸ γλώσσαις λαλεῖν, οὐχ ὡς ἐν μοίρᾳ χαρίσματος, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν
τάξει σημείου τοῖς πιστοῖς· καὶ δὴ καὶ προφητικὸν παρετίθει λόγιον οὕτως ἔχον "Ὅτι ἐν
ἑτερογλώσσοις "καὶ ἐν χείλεσιν ἑτέροις λαλήσω τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ, καὶ οὐδ' "ὡς
πιστεύσουσιν." ἐνεργεῖ δὲ διαφόρως ἐν ἑκάστῳ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὴν τῶν χαρισμάτων
διανομήν. ἵνα ὥσπερ, φησὶ, τὸ παχὺ δὴ τοῦτο καὶ ἀπὸ γῆς σῶμα συνέστηκεν ἐκ μορίων,
οὕτω καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἤτοι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, τουτέστιν ἡ Ἐκκλησία, διὰ πολλῆς ἁγίων
πληθύος εἰς ἑνότητα τὴν νοητὴν τελεωτάτην ἔχει τὴν σύστασιν. ταύτῃτοι καὶ ὁ
θεσπέσιος ∆αυεὶδ περιεστάλθαι φησὶν αὐτὴν "ἐν ἱματισμῷ διαχρύσῳ"
περιπεποικιλμένῳ, τὸ τῶν χαρισμάτων οἶμαι πολυειδὲς καὶ τίμιον ὡς ἔν γε τούτῳ
σημαίνων. Ὅτι τοίνυν ἔμελλον οἱ τῆς ὑφ' ἡλίῳ μυσταγωγοὶ γλώσσῃ 290 τε ἁπάσῃ καὶ
ἔθνει παντὶ προσλαλεῖν τὸ εὐαγγελικὸν δηλονότι καὶ σωτήριον κήρυγμα, σημεῖον
ἐδίδου τὰς γλώσσας αὐτοῖς· ἄνδρες ὄντες Γαλιλαῖοι καὶ τεθραμμένοι κατὰ τὴν
Ἰουδαίαν, Ἑβραῖοι τε καὶ ἐξ Ἑβραίων, Μήδοις τε καὶ Πάρθοις, καὶ μέντοι καὶ Ἐλαμίταις,

pass_a_gloss: [Continuing u04-rem-mid, ‘also the workings of the powers, that is’] the God-signs (θεοσημίαι) through the saints, the same God brings to completion (ἀποπεραίνω) for us; for all things, as I said, from Father through Son in Spirit, and upon all the things set right (κατορθόω) the holy and consubstantial Trinity is glorified. For look (ἀθρέω) how he begins from the Spirit as being in us and working the distribution of the divine gifts; and having made the account go up (ἀναβιβάζω) to the Son, who is Son according to nature, he goes up thus finally to the Father, assigning (προσνέμω) to him the working through the Spirit through the middle of the Son. [Lemma] And to another faith in the same Spirit. Faith in these words would be, as I suppose, the firm seat (ἑδραιότης) toward any whatever of the goods and of the things God might wish; for we say Moses the hierophant (ἱεροφάντης) became faithful thus ‘in his whole house’; for not the needing to believe only that by nature and truly one is God of all would be thought and called faith, but the having stood well (βεβηκέναι) in soul, ‘and to be ready for going with the Lord God’ according to the voice of the prophet; and indeed the inspired disciples approached once to Christ saying clearly, ‘Add (πρόσθες) to us faith.’ And there are given besides this also gifts of healings (ἰάματα) in the one Spirit. And again watch for me finely (ἐπιτηρέω λεπτῶς): for the Spirit being said to distribute the gifts of the healings, Christ is the giver; for he gave to the holy apostles ‘authority against unclean spirits so as to cast them out’; and indeed he said, ‘Heal the sick, and raise dead, cleanse lepers, and cast out demons; as a gift (δωρεάν) you received, as a gift give.’ And his altogether also the workings of the powers, but in the one Spirit; as Moses threw the rod to earth and it became a snake, he refashioned (μετασκευάζω) the rivers into blood, he led out water from rock; and the blessed prophets have accomplished very many things even beyond word and wonder; and these we say are the workings of the powers through the one Spirit; but also another one prophesies, but not without the Spirit; and someone has discernings (διακρίσεις) of spirits, but in the Spirit himself; of what sort of spirits has been said before; and he insists (ἰσχυρίζομαι) that to others also is given the knowing of kinds (γένη) of tongues, and indeed of interpretations (ἑρμηνεῖαι); and this we say is a proper (ἴδιος) gift, and supplied to some in season and need by way of dispensation (οἰκονομικῶς). But some were speaking in the tongues, though before not knowing them, others were understanding (σύνειμι), interpreting, though some formerly did not have the ear practiced (ἐντριβής) and in the habit of such; and the inspired Paul strongly asserts that to those then believers was given the speaking in tongues, not as in a portion (μοῖρα) of gift, but as in rank (τάξις) of sign; and indeed he set beside a prophetic oracle having thus: ‘Because in other-tongued (ἑτερόγλωσσοι) and in other lips I will speak to this people, and not even so will they believe.’ And the Spirit works differently in each the distribution of the gifts; so that as, he says, this thick (παχύς) body and from earth stands composed of parts, so also Christ, or (ἤτοι) his body, that is the Church, through a great multitude (πληθύς) of saints into the spiritual (νοητή) unity has its most perfect composition (σύστασις). For this reason also the inspired David says she has been wrapped about (περιστέλλω) ‘in raiment shot with gold,’ embroidered round about (περιποικίλλω), signifying, I think, the many-formed (πολυειδής) and precious of the gifts as in this. Since then the initiators (μυσταγωγοί) of [the earth] under the sun were going to speak to every tongue and every nation the gospel, clearly, and saving proclamation, he was giving them the tongues as a sign; being Galilean men and reared according to Judea, Hebrews and from Hebrews, to Medes and Parthians, and indeed also to Elamites, [continues at the start of u05-open].
pass_b_english: …the divine signs done through the saints, the same God accomplishes for us (1 Corinthians 12:6). For all things, as I said, are from the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and in everything that is well done the holy and consubstantial Trinity is glorified. For see how he begins from the Spirit, as the one who is in us and works the distribution of the divine gifts; then, raising his account to the Son, who is Son by nature, he goes up at last to the Father, ascribing to him, by way of the Son, the working done through the Spirit.

“To another, faith by the same Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:9). Faith here would be, as I think, steadfastness toward every good thing whatever, and toward whatever God may will. For in this sense we say that Moses, the revealer of holy things, was faithful “in all his house” (Hebrews 3:2; Numbers 12:7). For faith would not be understood or spoken of as only the duty to believe that by nature and in truth there is one God of all, but as standing firm in soul, “and being ready to walk with the Lord God,” in the words of the prophet (Micah 6:8). And so the inspired disciples once came to Christ, saying plainly, “Increase our faith” (Luke 17:5).

Besides this, gifts of healing are also given by the one Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:9). And again, mark this closely, I ask you: though the Spirit is said to distribute the gifts of healing, it is Christ who gives them. For he gave the holy apostles “authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out” (Matthew 10:1); and indeed he said, “Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. You received without cost; give without cost” (Matthew 10:8).

The workings of miracles are certainly his as well, but in the one Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:10). For instance, Moses threw his staff on the ground and it became a serpent (Exodus 4:3); he turned the rivers into blood (Exodus 7:20); he brought water out of the rock (Exodus 17:6). And the blessed prophets performed a great many deeds beyond words and beyond wonder. These, we say, are the workings of miracles through the one Spirit. Another, again, prophesies, but not apart from the Spirit; and someone has the discernment of spirits, but in the Spirit himself (1 Corinthians 12:10). What kind of spirits are meant has been said earlier.

Paul also insists that to others it is given to know kinds of tongues, and indeed their interpretation (1 Corinthians 12:10). This we call a gift of its own kind, supplied to some in God’s plan, at a set time and for a need. But some spoke in the tongues though they had not known them before, while others understood and interpreted them, though some of them had never before had an ear trained in such languages or used to them. Yet the inspired Paul firmly states that speaking in tongues was given to the believers of that time not as counted among the gifts but as ranking as a sign. And he set beside it a prophetic oracle that runs thus: “By people of strange tongues and by the lips of others I will speak to this people, and not even so will they believe” (1 Corinthians 14:21; Isaiah 28:11–12).

The Spirit works the distribution of the gifts differently in each (1 Corinthians 12:11), so that, as he says, just as this coarse body from the earth is made up of parts, so too Christ, or rather his body, that is, the Church, has its most perfect structure through a great multitude of saints joined into a spiritual unity (1 Corinthians 12:12, 27). For this reason the inspired David too says that she is clothed “in a garment woven with gold,” embroidered in many colors (Psalm 45:9), signifying by this, I think, how many and how precious the gifts are.

Because, then, those who were to lead the world under the sun into the mysteries were to speak the saving proclamation of the Gospel to every tongue and every nation, he gave them the tongues as a sign. Men of Galilee they were, brought up in Judea, Hebrews born of Hebrews (Acts 2:7; Philippians 3:5), and yet to Medes and Parthians, and indeed to Elamites (Acts 2:9)…

choices.why: Plain English for the title; the borrowed word would puzzle readers.

rejected: not as a mere share of grace, but as a sign-gift
choices.why: μοῖρα and τάξις are parallel nouns of class and rank.

choices.english: to the believers of that time
choices.why: Read with δεδόσθαι; fits 1 Corinthians 14:22. The other reading is given in a note.
The wording is Paul’s form of Isaiah 28:11–12.
